architecture.mechanism: CMOS chips provide enhanced miniaturization, parallel sensing, and low power consumption, enabling a plurality of parallel sensing modalities (electrical, magnetic, mechanical) that transduce physical events into the electrical domain so that one failed channel can be outvoted by the others.
architecture.intervention: Integrate a CMOS-based multi-modal shifter-position sensor array (electrical contact sensing plus magnetic and mechanical sensing channels) into the electronic shifter assembly, with the parallel channels feeding a fault-tolerant shifter control unit that cross-checks modalities and commands a fail-safe state when any single channel disagrees, so steering and braking authority is never handed off to a faulty shifter path.
architecture.expected_effect: During an electronic shifter malfunction (buzzing, flashing, loss of position report), the redundant CMOS channels continue to supply valid position data or force a safe default state, preserving steering and braking control instead of losing them.
architecture.falsification_test: On a shifter assembly test bench, inject single-point faults (open circuit, short-to-ground, EMI burst, debounced contact chatter) into individual sensing channels while cycling the shifter through Park/Reverse/Neutral/Drive; the design is falsified if steering or braking control is lost, position error exceeds specification, or the assembly fails to enter its fail-safe state within the documented time limit.
